subject: Physics
subtopic: Newton's first law and free-body diagrams
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

must_contain: A case that keeps moving after the push has ended.
A case at rest with no change in motion, treated by the same rule.

controlled_variation.vary: whether a brief push is still in contact
controlled_variation.hold: the cart's direction and an approximately frictionless surface after release
controlled_variation.notice: the cart can continue moving after the applied push becomes zero

controlled_variation.vary: the initial velocity from zero to nonzero
controlled_variation.notice: both rest and steady motion fit the same zero-change condition

must_contain: At least two nonzero force arrows whose vector sum is zero.
A comparison between 'no force' and 'zero net force'.

controlled_variation.vary: the magnitudes of two opposite collinear forces together
controlled_variation.notice: the individual arrows can grow while the net arrow remains zero

must_contain: The same interaction shown on two separate body diagrams.
A rule that every arrow on one diagram must name an external agent acting on that chosen body.

controlled_variation.vary: which interacting body is isolated
controlled_variation.notice: the equal-and-opposite partner arrow moves to the other body's diagram rather than cancelling on one diagram

controlled_variation.vary: an additional external horizontal force on one body
controlled_variation.hold: the same contact between the two bodies
controlled_variation.notice: the two bodies can have different net forces even though the two partner forces remain equal and opposite

must_contain: A named contact surface and a relative-sliding or slip-tendency statement.
A conveyor-belt counterexample where friction need not point opposite the object's ground-frame velocity.
An explicit case where rough surfaces are in contact but the friction force is zero because no tangential force is required.

controlled_variation.vary: the belt speed relative to the box
controlled_variation.notice: friction direction follows relative slip tendency at the contact

controlled_variation.vary: the object's ground-frame motion direction
controlled_variation.notice: friction is not defined by the object's velocity alone

controlled_variation.vary: whether the contact has a tangential slip tendency at all
controlled_variation.notice: rough contact can support friction without requiring a nonzero friction force in every state

must_contain: One chosen body with all signed external forces summed before using F = ma.
A zero-net-force boundary that recovers zero acceleration.

controlled_variation.vary: the signed net external force
controlled_variation.notice: acceleration changes in direct proportion and follows the net-force sign

controlled_variation.vary: the mass
controlled_variation.notice: larger mass gives smaller acceleration magnitude

must_contain: A no-slip friction requirement compared against the static limit.
An explicit case where static friction is below its maximum.
A normal reaction obtained from the actual FBD rather than assumed equal to mg.
A contact-state decision that refuses to choose static-limit or kinetic-friction equality merely because a coefficient is supplied.

controlled_variation.vary: the applied tangential force below the slip threshold
controlled_variation.hold: the same contact, N and mu_s
controlled_variation.notice: static friction changes to match the required no-slip value while remaining below its limit

controlled_variation.vary: the contact state from impending slip to established sliding
controlled_variation.hold: the same surface pair and normal reaction
controlled_variation.notice: the governing relation changes from the static threshold to the kinetic model

controlled_variation.vary: an applied force component perpendicular to the contact
controlled_variation.hold: mass, friction coefficients and contact state logic
controlled_variation.notice: the normal reaction must be solved from the actual perpendicular dynamics before any friction limit is evaluated

must_contain: A physical statement of the connection that fixes relative separation.
One signed Newton-II equation per body before any system-level cancellation.
A whole-system check that removes only internal partner forces.

controlled_variation.vary: whether the connection/contact remains active
controlled_variation.hold: the same two bodies and external forces
controlled_variation.notice: the common-acceleration relation disappears when the constraint is lost

controlled_variation.vary: whether the bodies are solved separately or as one system
controlled_variation.notice: the internal force is present in body equations but cancels from the combined system sum

must_contain: An explicit ideal-string/redirection model declaration before one common T is used.
Separate tension arrows on the body-specific FBDs.
A nonideal boundary where equal tension is refused.

controlled_variation.vary: which attached body is isolated
controlled_variation.notice: the tension magnitude stays T while the force arrow belongs to the selected body and follows its local string direction

controlled_variation.vary: the pulley from ideal to explicitly frictional
controlled_variation.hold: the same two bodies and rope path
controlled_variation.notice: equal tension is no longer guaranteed by the bounded model

must_contain: Coordinates declared along the two string segments.
The fixed-length equation y_A + y_B = constant.
The derived signed acceleration relation a_A + a_B = 0.
A boundary case that forces re-derivation when the pulley itself moves.

controlled_variation.vary: which end moves farther from the fixed pulley
controlled_variation.hold: the same taut inextensible string and coordinate convention
controlled_variation.notice: the other straight segment shortens by the same amount

controlled_variation.vary: the pulley from fixed to movable
controlled_variation.notice: the old two-segment length equation is no longer sufficient and must be rebuilt

must_contain: The same interaction named twice as A-on-B and B-on-A.
Equal-and-opposite partner arrows placed on different body diagrams.

controlled_variation.vary: which body is selected for the free-body diagram
controlled_variation.notice: only the force acting on the selected body appears in that diagram

controlled_variation.vary: the strength of the interaction
controlled_variation.hold: the same two bodies and interaction
controlled_variation.notice: both partner magnitudes change together while remaining opposite

must_contain: Two observers describing the same object, one in a non-accelerating frame and one in an accelerating frame.
An explicit declaration of the chosen frame before the force sum is written.

controlled_variation.vary: the observer from roadside to steadily moving bus
controlled_variation.hold: the physical interactions and the bus's zero acceleration
controlled_variation.notice: no extra force is needed when the frames differ only by constant velocity

controlled_variation.vary: the bus from steady speed to forward acceleration
controlled_variation.hold: the same object and physical interactions

family.invariant_demand: Choose the body and frame, identify only forces acting on that body, add them as directed quantities, decide any contact/connection model explicitly, and use the resulting force and kinematic constraints to determine acceleration.
family.difficult_move: Choosing the correct physical boundary and model before writing equations: body ownership for forces, contact state for friction, and only geometry-justified acceleration/tension constraints for connected bodies.
family.independent_check: Every force arrow names an external agent acting on the chosen body; static friction satisfies its inequality, system-level cancellation respects the chosen boundary, and any string acceleration relation can be reconstructed from the declared fixed-length geometry.

support_ladder.handed_over: The target body, coordinate directions, and a list of candidate interactions are supplied.
The target body and coordinate directions are supplied.
Only the physical situation and requested acceleration or force are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: The problem is described from inside an accelerating vehicle and the learner must choose an inertial-frame analysis or add a pseudo-force.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the chosen observer frame is inertial

transfer.changed_demand: A contact-and-motion sketch must be converted into separate free-body diagrams before any equations are written.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which interactions act on each chosen body

transfer.changed_demand: Two connected bodies must be analysed with one free-body diagram per body and the shared interaction linked across the equations.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which equal-and-opposite forces belong to different equations

transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the contact is static, impending slip, or already sliding

transfer.changed_demand: Two bodies are linked but the problem does not state whether they should be solved separately or as one system.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which connection creates a shared acceleration and where internal-force cancellation is legitimate

transfer.information_not_handed_over: which straight string segments vary and what coordinate signs they use
